questions.q: What is the main idea of the Von Neumann architecture?
options: Programs are stored only on the hard disk
Every instruction is processed by a separate computer
Programs and data are stored together in main memory and instructions are fetched one at a time
Data is never stored in memory

questions.q: Which change would most help a CPU to run several tasks at the same time?
options: Using a longer keyboard cable
Adding more USB ports
Adding more cores
Using a bigger monitor

questions.q: Which is an advantage of an SSD compared with an HDD?
options: Faster access to data and no moving parts
It stores data on spinning magnetic disks
It is always cheaper per gigabyte
It always has a larger capacity

questions.q: What does a compiler do?
options: Runs the program one line at a time
Translates the whole program into machine code before it is run
Checks the spelling of comments
Stores the program in RAM

questions.q: What is the job of a device driver?
options: To protect the computer from viruses
To let the operating system communicate with a piece of hardware
To compress files
To increase the amount of RAM

questions.q: What is virtual memory?
options: Part of secondary storage used as extra memory when RAM is full
A faster type of cache
Memory that exists only inside the CPU
Memory that never loses its data

questions.q: The program counter holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched.
An interpreter translates and runs a program one line at a time.
Firmware is software stored on a device, for example in a router, that controls how it works.
Cache memory is slower than RAM.
questions.explain: Cache is faster than RAM, which is why it is placed close to the CPU.

questions.q: The ____ is the part of the CPU that performs arithmetic and logic operations.
A ____ translates a high-level program into machine code in one go.
Very fast memory built into or very close to the CPU that stores frequently used data is called ____ memory.
Instructions are stored in main memory as ____ code, which is made of 1s and 0s.
Explain how increasing the amount of RAM can improve a computer's performance.
questions.answer: More programs and data can be held in RAM at once (1); so the computer uses slow secondary storage / virtual memory less often (1).

questions.q: Give two differences between an HDD and an SSD.
questions.answer: Any two from: HDD has moving parts but SSD has none; SSD is faster to read/write; SSD is quieter and uses less power; HDD is usually cheaper per gigabyte.

questions.q: Describe the role of the control unit and the ALU in the CPU.
questions.answer: The control unit fetches and decodes instructions and coordinates the other parts (1); the ALU carries out calculations and logical comparisons (1).

questions.q: Match each CPU part to its job.
pairs: Tiny, very fast storage inside the CPU

questions.q: Match each translator to its description.
pairs: Translates the whole program at once into machine code
Translates and runs the program line by line
Translates assembly language into machine code
The binary instructions the CPU can run directly

questions.q: Match each item to its description.
pairs: Software stored permanently on a hardware device to control it
Lets the operating system work with a device such as a printer
Copies files so they can be restored later
